title: DDDDC
statementMd:
While preparing a problem for the 3D(C4)3D(C4) contest, Emanuel became interested in abbreviations. Some seem intuitive to him, while others do not. He has asked you to write a program to tell them apart.

A string 𝑡t is an *intuitive abbreviation* of a string 𝑠s if 𝑡t can be obtained by deleting zero or more characters from 𝑠s without changing the order of the remaining characters. Each occurrence of a letter in 𝑡t must correspond to a distinct occurrence in 𝑠s.

For example, `DDDDC` is an intuitive abbreviation of `DIRTYDEEDSDONEDIRTCHEAP`, and `DCC` is an intuitive abbreviation of `DINOSSAUROCODECUP`.

For each test case, determine whether the second string is an intuitive abbreviation of the first.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑞q (1≤𝑞≤1051≤q≤105), the number of test cases.

Each test case consists of one line containing two space-separated strings 𝑠s and 𝑡t (1≤|𝑠|,|𝑡|≤1051≤|s|,|t|≤105). Both strings consist only of uppercase English letters.

The sum of the lengths of all strings 𝑠s and 𝑡t does not exceed 106106.

## Output

For each test case, print `SIM` (Portuguese for "yes") if 𝑡t is an intuitive abbreviation of 𝑠s, or `NAO` ("no") otherwise.

samples.input:
8
DCCCODECUP DCCCC
DCCCODECUP DDDDC
DIRTYDEEDSDONEDIRTCHEAP DDDDC
MVKAIO MK
HIGINOH HGH
DCCCCC DCCCC
ESTADOSUNIDOS EEUU
TREINAMENTOPARAAMARATONA TREM
samples.output:

NAO
